turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Palabra BCS reports the state planning ministry has begun a 48 million peso paving project on Francisco King Rondero street in La Paz.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The work started on 11 November between Ignacio Altamirano and México streets and adds new water and sewer lines.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: It will serve more than 13,000 residents in El Esterito and Ladrillera with hydraulic concrete, storm-water walls and solar lighting.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: On the same day PVTIME noted CFE opened tenders for the Oasis project in Mulegé.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That plan calls for 72 MW of solar.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It includes 80 MWh of battery storage.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Plus a 20 MW electrolyser for green hydrogen.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The project is expected to power roughly 40,000 households.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And it would cut about 94,000 tonnes of CO2 each year.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: [pause] The portal lists a 2023 grid peak of 660 MW net for the state.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: This is Radio BCS2050 and our topic is infrastructure.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The question we will answer is how these projects will affect daily service and costs for residents by 2050.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: [chuckle] That is the part worth tracking closely.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Palabra BCS reports that state planning ministry crews will start paving Francisco King Rondero street in La Paz on 11 November.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The project carries a 48 million peso price tag and runs between Ignacio Altamirano and México streets.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Residents along that corridor have dealt with worn pavement and unreliable water service for years.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The timing lines up with the report date of 10 November from Palabra BCS.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Workers will lay hydraulic concrete while they replace the old water and sewer lines.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Those lines will go straight to the La Paz water utility once the work finishes.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: How many of those homes still deal with low water pressure today?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That remains one of the open questions the utility will have to answer after handover.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The same contract adds storm-water walls, accessible sidewalks and solar lighting.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: More than 13,000 residents in El Esterito and Ladrillera stand to gain from the upgrades.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: I keep thinking about how the new sidewalks will change daily walks for families there.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Exactly, and the solar lights should cut evening safety concerns along the route.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Hydraulic concrete should hold up longer against coastal traffic than older surfaces.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It also pairs well with the new storm-water walls during heavy rain seasons. [pause]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Now shift to Mulegé. PVTIME says CFE opened tenders for the Oasis microgrid project on 9 November.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The package includes 72 megawatts of solar panels and 80 megawatt-hours of battery storage.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: A 20-megawatt electrolyser will turn surplus solar power into green hydrogen.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The system is sized to serve about 40,000 households across the region.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: It is also expected to cut roughly 94,000 tonnes of carbon dioxide each year.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: HDF Energy is listed as the partner on the tender documents.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What happens if the hydrogen storage portion runs behind schedule?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That is still uncertain because the tender only closed recently.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The electrolyser approach lets extra daytime solar get stored for night use.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That design choice could help rural spots in Mulegé avoid frequent outages.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Meanwhile Meganoticias reports that Los Cabos public services need a full week to restore normal rubbish collection.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Heavy rains damaged the unpaved streets and rural roads again, leaving silt everywhere.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The worst-hit areas include Gastélum, Tierra y Libertad, Mesa Colorada, El Zacatal and Guaymitas.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Officials note this is the eighth or ninth time they have rebuilt those same stretches.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Does the repeated damage point to a deeper drainage problem?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It does, and the city has not yet released a longer-term fix.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So three infrastructure stories landed in the same week, each touching daily life in different parts of the state.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Yes, and the common thread is how quickly small delays in roads or power can affect entire neighbourhoods. [chuckle]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Palabra BCS reports that the state planning ministry will start paving Francisco King Rondero street in La Paz on 11 November.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: They will spend 48 million pesos on hydraulic concrete plus new water and sewer lines.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The work runs between Ignacio Altamirano and México streets and will reach over 13,000 residents.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Really? That includes neighbourhoods like El Esterito and Ladrillera.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The lines will be handed to the La Paz water utility along with storm-water walls and solar lighting.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Accessible sidewalks are also part of the plan, which should help daily movement there.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Wait—does that mean residents see both street repairs and better drainage at once?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Exactly. One project bundles the pavement, pipes and lighting for those blocks.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: PVTIME reports that CFE opened a tender for the Oasis microgrid project in Mulegé.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The project includes 72 megawatts of solar plus 80 megawatt-hours of batteries.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: It also adds a 20-megawatt electrolyser to store surplus power as green hydrogen.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: HDF Energy is working with CFE on this tender.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The system is expected to supply about 40,000 households.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It would avoid roughly 94,000 tonnes of CO2 each year.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So the electricity could reach places beyond Mulegé itself if the grid links up.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That ties into the inland needs we see elsewhere. [chuckle]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Loreto is described in the portal as a mid-peninsula tourism and conservation node.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Its strengths include the POEL 2014 plan and the second stage of the wastewater plant plus the Londó-Loreto aqueduct.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The constraints remain seasonal water demand and a thinner labor market.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: How does the aqueduct change daily supply for residents there?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: It moves water from Londó to support tourism without drawing only on local sources.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Comondú is positioned as an inland agri and service hub with pilots for desalination and irrigation.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The portal notes UABCS work on a clean desalination MIA and ongoing irrigation projects.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Aquifer stress and energy needs for pumping stay the main limits there.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So the paving in La Paz ties directly to water reliability for those neighborhoods.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The Mulegé tender shows how renewable storage could support inland hubs like Comondú over time.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Loreto’s aqueduct and plant upgrades fit the same pattern of linking water to conservation goals.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The open question is how the PMDU now in progress will set the next investment order. [pause] These projects show where the lines between daily service and long-term planning meet.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Meganoticias reported last week that the design for a bridge over the San José Viejo arroyo is finished and the governor has asked the federal transport ministry for funds to build it next year.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That arroyo floods every rainy season and cuts off neighborhoods from the airport road.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The same outlet also covered how altered stream beds and missing storm drains sent eighteen tonnes of waste onto El Médano beach after the October rains.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Hundreds of tyres came with it too.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The shoulders are taking the worst hit.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Meanwhile Tribuna de México says Mulegé spent 713 million pesos on public works over five years.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Of that total, 215 million went to water lines and sewers.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: They have also started the first seven kilometres of a new aqueduct from Palo Verde to Santa Rosalía.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Yet the same story notes federal funding for those works dropped 70 percent.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Quepoca adds that the second desalination plant in Cabo San Lucas is 75 percent complete.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It will add 250 litres per second once it finishes.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The portal's earlier Foresight editions already flagged water-energy coupling as the real ceiling for 2050.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Exactly. The desal plants depend on the grid staying up.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The knowledge graph lists that coupling as a signal rather than a solved capacity.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: So the bridge, the drains, the highway repairs and the new aqueduct all sit on the same hidden thread.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: One break in the power supply and the desal output drops, the pumps for the new sewers stop, and runoff problems get worse.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The graph also records hurricanes Polo and Rachel as a shared risk across Comondú, Mulegé, Los Cabos and La Paz, including the power grid itself.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Yet none of the recent project stories mention grid hardening. [pause]

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The surprise is that the 70 percent federal cut in Mulegé happened even while local spending on water works reached 215 million pesos.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That leaves the municipalities and the state carrying most of the load on drainage, paving and aqueduct stages.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Sepuimm still ranks paving by traffic volume first, then flood zones, hospitals and schools.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So the hidden design is really a chain: water supply needs power, power needs storm protection, and storm protection needs the drains and bridges that keep the roads open.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The foresight questions already ask whether the east cape edge and La Paz capital can grow without solving that chain first.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: We still do not know how the new desal plant will handle the next outage. [chuckle]

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Or whether the remaining 25 percent of the plant will be finished before the federal term ends.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The portal's energy data shows the transmission line from La Paz to Los Cabos is limited to about 237 MW.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Really? That seems low compared to what the region actually needs.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Exactly.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: What does the peak demand look like then?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: On 10 September 2024 at 15:45 the system hit an instant peak of 688.5 MW according to PAMRNT records.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: So the line can only carry roughly one-third of that peak demand.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Think of it like a two-lane road trying to handle eight lanes of rush-hour traffic.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: [chuckle] That explains the tension on the 115 kV lines mentioned in the same guide.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The portal lists the same 237 MW limit repeatedly across different documents.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: What happens when demand keeps climbing past that number?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The guide points to CENACE alerts around 688.5–689 MW for 2024.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Already past the line capacity.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Yes, and the portal notes no other major transmission routes are listed for that stretch.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: So Los Cabos relies on that single corridor for most of its power.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The 2024 peak was below the listed maximum of 689 MW.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: One number away from the documented ceiling.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The same energy files also record an earlier peak of 660 MW in 2023.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It has been climbing steadily each year.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Another reading shows 675 MW later that same year.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The portal leaves open how the system will handle the next jump without new lines.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: I keep wondering what a resident in Cabo San Lucas notices first when the lights flicker during peak hours.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Probably the hotels dimming the AC right when tourists expect it most.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The guide does not spell out daily outages, but the numbers sit right at the edge.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: So any new resort or housing project would push the same line harder.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: [pause] That bottleneck feels like the hidden piece behind every new hotel or house.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The Base de datos BCS 2050 ontology lists a viability package that ties any large project to water sources, energy supply, planning instruments and land restrictions.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That package names desal plants, hotels, industrial parks, housing and roads together.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: It also names the specific agencies that must be consulted before any decision.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Really? Water checks go to DMA, the aquifers and CONAGUA.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Energy checks go to SIBCS, CFE and the PRODESEN plan.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Planning instruments listed are POERBCS and the municipal PDU or PSDU.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Restrictions include protected natural areas, coastal zones and land tenure questions.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The portal's knowledge graph adds a signal on water-energy coupling. [chuckle]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That signal notes urban supply in Los Cabos and La Paz depends on the power grid.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: A second signal records that hurricanes Polo and Rachel can hit the same grid across several municipalities.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The same graph shows no actual project node yet for the Oasis hydrogen idea in Mulegé.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It only records the question of whether that corridor would use local water.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Library documents already in the system include Douglas Farr's 2008 guide on sustainable urbanism for arid places.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: They also list the ITDP 2018 streets guide for walking and cycling networks.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And the 2015 Tactical Urbanism manual for low-cost tests of public space.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: All three sit alongside the viability questions in the same database.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What remains uncertain is which of these factors will actually move first on any given site.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The mesas de trabajo tracked in the portal include one on infrastructure and energy run by SEPUIMM.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Another covers water with CEA and CONAGUA, based on notes from 30 sep 2026.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Urban design questions for Los Cabos sit with IMPLAN.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Those tables are where the coupled factors get tested, [pause] at least on paper.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The portal's Vision pillar for infrastructure centers on energy, and the documented finding is that Baja California Sur stays locked as an island grid.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Right. The risk listed is that the power ceiling remains one number, and tourism growth plus desalination both draw from the same system.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: SIBCS hit a peak of 689 MW in 2024.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That leaves almost no headroom anywhere else.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The portal also records 660 MW net for 2023.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: And 675 MW as well.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The aspiration is a system that finally steps past island status, with clean generation and storage sized to the actual ceiling.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The Trend 2050 describes a polycentric layout instead of repeating the same coastal model from south to north.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Los Cabos keeps the tourism engine but under water and power stress.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: East Cape stays in tension with protected areas.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Todos Santos and El Pescadero form the Pacific amenity spine.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: La Paz acts as the service capital and water-energy node.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Loreto serves as a tourism-conservation anchor.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Comondú holds the agricultural hub role with more room, and northern Mulegé runs as a thinly documented corridor.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The remote-generation tender there is already visible.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The portal lists four conditions that would have to hold for that pattern to work.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Each area keeps its distinct role rather than spreading Cabos-style development statewide.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: New tourism or residential growth only where water and energy show documented margin, or through non-DMA sources like desal without claiming NOM-011 credit.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: East Cape and Loreto must respect ANP and POEL ceilings before any scaling of hospitality.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Comondú and the north can add production and energy, but without draining services or protected zones.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The watchlist items are SIBCS reliability against CFE works and OOMSAPAS supply incidents, plus the CFE Oasis Mulegé tender.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That tender covers 72 MW PV.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: It also includes 20 MW over 80 MWh of storage.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: And a 20 MW electrolyser.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The levers named are completing those northern tenders transparently, planning desal and pumping inside the grid from the start, and refusing added Cabos demand without proven margin.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Energy showed zero items in the current week, with EWMA at 1.66 and direction flat. [chuckle]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So the Trend already flags the series as insufficient where data stops short of 2050 peaks.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: What would it take to shift from the risk to the aspiration, in practice?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Transparent award of the Mulegé tender and coordinated planning so desalination does not simply add missing megawatts later.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: State planning ministry work on Francisco King Rondero street in La Paz now includes new water and sewer lines along the paving.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That project shows local authorities taking direct steps on basic services.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: CFE has opened tenders for the Oasis project in Mulegé covering solar generation, battery storage and green hydrogen.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: SICT says the design for the San José Viejo arroyo bridge is complete.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Really? And Mulegé has begun the new Palo Verde–Santa Rosalía aqueduct while overall federal works funding dropped.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Los Cabos faces repeated highway damage from rain and sewage spills, plus waste flowing into the sea from altered stream beds.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Los Cabos will need time to fix rubbish collection because damaged dirt roads block access.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The changes mean steadier water service and cleaner energy options for some towns, but responsibility stays split among state, federal and municipal offices. [pause]

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: What remains unknown is how quickly the new bridge and aqueduct will finish and whether funding gaps will slow other repairs.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: I keep wondering how residents will feel once the La Paz street work is done. [chuckle]
